statements.text: We’re not opposed to data centers. We just want to make sure that if we’re going to put a data center on a federal facility, that federal facility is not going to be degraded by the data center.

statements.text: What are the energy issues? What are the water issues as it applies to the base? Is there backup power, is there light, noise pollution that would harm the utility of that base? Is there encroachment on training and operations and the physical and supply chain of security?

statements.text: As we enter the period of AI, which requires very serious data centers, data facilities, that are extraordinary consumers of both energy and water, the question arises as to whether they should be on military bases.
statements.venue: E&E News article on NDAA amendment about data centers on military bases

statements.text:
The Pentagon is moving quickly to lease land on military bases for massive AI data centers, but too often the extraordinary demand for energy and water comes at the expense of surrounding communities.

That is why I introduced legislation requiring the DOD to fully evaluate the impacts before any deal is finalized.
